procedure: Make three small holes at different heights in the side of a container.
Observe the water streams flowing out of the holes. Notice that each stream initially flows out normal to the surface before curving down due to gravity.
Compare the distances at which the streams hit the ground. Identify which stream hits the ground at the larger distance.
Determine at which position the liquid has more pressure.
aim: To observe how liquid pressure changes with depth.

viva.question: How does liquid pressure change with depth?
Which hole has the greatest liquid pressure?
In which direction does water initially flow out of a hole in the side of the container?
Why do the water streams curve down after leaving the holes?
Which stream is expected to hit the ground at the larger distance?
viva.answer: The stream from the lowest hole.

apparatus: Nail or pin for making the holes
diagram: Draw a container filled with water and three holes at different heights in its side; show the water streams flowing out and curving down, and label the container contents “WATER”, the upper region “LOWEST PRESSURE”, and the lower region “HIGHEST PRESSURE”.
title: Pressure in liquids at different depths
precautions: Make the three holes small and at clearly different heights.
Keep the container steady while filling it and observing the streams.
Observe the streams from a safe distance and keep the area around the container clear.
Avoid splashing water onto electrical equipment or the floor.
result: The stream from the lowest hole hits the ground at the larger distance. This shows that liquid pressure increases with depth.
